items.title: All catalogs.* carry RLS
items.evidence: CLOSED 2026-07-29: migration 202608100000 applied_held + applied_on_prod:true (owner #3549). LIVE Neon: catalogs.account_types + wo_cancellation_reasons both relrowsecurity+relforcerowsecurity true, 3 policies each, 0 DELETE policies, ih35_app INSERT/SELECT/UPDATE only. WRITE-AUTHZ ONLY (global catalogs — not entity-scoping). Guard verify-lst-rls01-global-catalog-write-authz-closed (step 1780). | BUILT AND HELD 2026-07-25 as #3549 — stays FAIL until the owner Neon-applies it. Migration 202608100000_lst_rls_01_global_catalog_write_authz.sql, registered HELD without applied_on_prod (absence = not-applied). VERDICT — both tables are SHARED-CANONICAL/GLOBAL, so this is WRITE-AUTHZ ONLY and deliberately NOT entity scoping. catalogs.account_types (202606080010:16-27) and catalogs.wo_cancellation_reasons (202606221200:31-37) have NO operating_company_id, RLS OFF, ZERO policies. 202607011700:5-13 states the locked model verbatim: account_types is a GLOBAL reference and the entity boundary sits on detail_types.operating_company_id, not on the shared type. Company-scoping all-NULL rows under FORCE RLS would return ZERO rows and break account-type-catalog.routes.ts:70-83, whose join already reads dt.operating_company_id IS NULL OR = $1 precisely because the parent is shared. Choosing scoping here would have been an outage, not a fix. WHAT WAS ACTUALLY EXPOSED, proved pre-fix in a throwaway container as a Dispatcher-role session: INSERT of a rogue account type succeeded; UPDATE HIJACKED the BANK type; DELETE destroyed a WO reason and an account type. Both tables were fully writable and deletable by any role. EXTRA DEFECT FOUND: catalogs carries ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES granting DELETE to ih35_app (0065:48, 0116:45-46), and both tables were created after those ran — so DELETE reached account_types even though its own GRANT never names it. A narrower GRANT cannot fix that; the migration REVOKEs DELETE explicitly. Same landmine documented at 202607420000:80-82. POST-FIX in-container: RLS enabled AND forced, 3 policies each, ZERO delete policies, effective privs INSERT,SELECT,UPDATE. Dispatcher INSERT and DELETE blocked; owner INSERT/UPDATE allowed, owner DELETE blocked; lucia bypass reads. NO READ REGRESSION — counts identical pre/post and the detail_types FK insert still succeeds across FORCE RLS. Applied twice = silent no-op; applied to an empty DB with no catalogs schema = skip, exit 0, no RAISE (fresh-CI safe). GUARD: verify-step 1520 — FAILS on origin/main with 12 issues (6 per table: no ENABLE RLS, no FORCE RLS, no SELECT policy, no INSERT policy, no UPDATE policy, no REVOKE DELETE), passes post-fix, selftest catches 9 mutations. It also pins the ANTI-OUTAGE half: it fails if any future migration adds operating_company_id or an app.operating_company_id predicate to either table, so the scoping mistake cannot be made later. SCOPE NOTE: catalogs.cancellation_reasons is named in the LST-RLS-01 audit but deliberately excluded — it is the legacy load-cancel catalog being retired by LST-LINK-01 / 202607940000 on another in-flight branch, and securing it here would clash. CI: locked-guards PASS (that is what executes the ~250 verify-steps incl. 1520), required-checks-gate PASS, rls-migration-scan PASS. hold-merge-gate FAILS BY DESIGN — PROTECTED until JORGE-APPROVED. UNVERIFIED: everything about prod. No DB access; no prod row count, RLS state or grant is claimed. Owner Neon-applies, then ledger-backfills. RE-CONFIRMED LIVE (CC-3 2026-08-29, healthz 14daeed): pg_policy read on br-fancy-credit-akjnd07a confirms catalogs.account_types and catalogs.wo_cancellation_reasons both still relrowsecurity=true, relforcerowsecurity=true, 3 policies each, 0 DELETE policies today -- the CLOSED/applied state (not the earlier HELD/UNVERIFIED text also present in this evidence blob from before the migration was applied) is what live prod actually shows.

items.title: Inline create is the first row INSIDE the dropdown, not an outside button
items.evidence: VERIFIED PASS 2026-07-28. CostBreakdownBox's Section B item picker and its sub-row PART picker were each a bare SelectCombobox with a separate '+ Create' BUTTON beside them — VERIFY-2/§7 require inline create as the first row INSIDE the dropdown. Section A of the SAME component already used ReferenceSelect, so this was never a design question: two sections of one box shipped with different grammars for the same act. Both migrated to ReferenceSelect (createKind='item', addNewLabel '+ Add new item' / '+ Add new part'), with the created record selected onto THAT line and, for parts, its label carried into the row description exactly as picking an existing part does. A THIRD offender was found by the guard after its detector was fixed: Section A's own fallback branch (rendered when operatingCompanyId is absent) also had an external '+ Create'. That control was removed rather than relocated — without an operating company a scoped catalog row cannot be created, so the honest UI is no create control, not a button with nowhere to write. The now-unused onQuickCreateCategory prop was NOT deleted (callers still pass it); it fires on inline create instead. Guard 1695 matches the SHAPE (a create button that is a sibling of a picker, nearest-picker-wins) rather than file names, so a future consumer written the same way is caught. Frontend form suite 8 failed/73 passed BOTH with and without the change (pre-existing, measured by stashing).

items.title: Guard-suite integrity: unique step numbers + no unwired guards
items.evidence: VERIFIED PASS 2026-07-28 — the UNIQUENESS/REGISTRATION half is now enforced; the unwired-guard half is NOT claimed (see below). Measured live: 922 step files, 807 numbered groups, 87 collision groups (the manifest's 87, independently reproduced). TWO ASSERTIONS OF DELIBERATELY DIFFERENT STRENGTH: (1) REGISTRATION — every numbered step's number must be in CLAIMED-NUMBERS.json. FULLY ENFORCED with ZERO grandfathering, because all 807 already satisfy it; there was nothing to exempt and no reason to weaken it. (2) UNIQUENESS — no NEW duplicate. The 87 historical groups are frozen in scripts/verify-step-number-historical-collisions.json for ONE specific reason: renaming them would invalidate the `GUARD: scripts/verify-steps/NNN-` references already recorded in MERGED commits, destroying the very traceability this protects. That is the same treatment verify-migration-filenames gives its 17 historical migration pairs — repo precedent, not a new exemption. The frozen list is kept HONEST: a listed group that stops colliding FAILS the guard, so the list can only shrink. Guard 1697 proven against the real tree — planting a duplicate 1714 exits 1 naming both files; removing it returns exit 0. Selftest covers clean, new duplicate, unregistered, and stale-freeze. NOT CLAIMED: the manifest's second half — guards that are package.json-only and executed by no workflow. scripts/.guard-exempt.json is a keyed object, not the 336-entry list the manifest describes, so that number could not be reproduced and the sub-item stays open rather than being asserted.

items.title: Catalog inventory reconciled: every catalogs.* table classified
items.evidence: VERIFIED PASS 2026-07-28 — the ENUMERATION and CLASSIFICATION deliverable is done; 37 tables are reported as awaiting an owner ruling rather than silently classified. Live (pg_class/pg_stat_all_tables, role-safe): 114 catalogs.* base tables. Route resolution required TWO corrections: name-equality between hub catalogKey and table name is WRONG (keys are kebab-case ROUTE SEGMENTS, e.g. 'brands' -> fuel_brands), and a proximity-window parse of the backend configs mis-attributed pairs (it produced equipment-types -> trailer_statuses, the same window-bleed class as the schema-parity bug fixed in #3715). Rebuilt with BALANCED-BRACE object parsing plus a second pass for explicitly-registered route files: 52 factory pairs + 11 explicit = 62 route->table mappings, zero conflicts. RESULT: 61 of 114 tables are routed (all 61 also appear on a hub tile — no routed-but-hidden catalog), 53 have no route (23 with rows, 30 empty). Classified 61 ROUTED, 14 HEADLESS-BY-DESIGN (audit_event_types, catalog_registry, fmcsa_lookups, file_categories, us_states, mexico_states, chart_of_accounts_seeds and similar system lookups), 2 RETIRE (cancellation_reasons — superseded by load_cancellation_reasons, must NEVER gain an editable route; ifta_states — retired in #3698), and 37 UNCLASSIFIED. Guard 1699 enforces what is enforceable today WITHOUT a database: every backend-routed catalog must have a ROUTED entry (a newly routed catalog with no ruling FAILS), and no RETIRE or HEADLESS table may be routed — the ifta_states hazard in guard form. It deliberately REPORTS the 37 unclassified on every run instead of failing on them, because failing CI would pressure someone into rubber-stamping 37 judgements to get green.
